proposals.title: Purpose and Use of This Document
proposals.statement: This document provides the reusable templates and checklists required to apply the SDD Architecture Governance Framework consistently.

proposals.title: Purpose and Use of This Document
proposals.statement: The templates shall be used pragmatically and proportionally.

proposals.title: Purpose and Use of This Document
proposals.statement: The templates should be tailored according to architecture impact, criticality, integration risk, security relevance and release relevance.

proposals.title: Purpose and Use of This Document
proposals.statement: However, tailoring should not remove the core governance information: business driver, architecture decision, process implication, ownership, evidence and follow-up action.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: The table below defines the minimum information required to make such a decision traceable and reviewable.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: Process implication | Explains what must happen in planning, delivery, verification, release or governance because of the decision. | Required review, test, integration step, release rule, governance process, exception process, quality gate, DevSecOps pipeline change

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: Review date | Defines when or under which condition the decision must be reassessed. | Review date, expiry condition, trigger event, next release, solution baseline change, guardrail update

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: The template should be completed with enough detail to make the decision understandable, reviewable and actionable.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: It should not become a long report for every minor design choice.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: The level of detail should be proportional to the impact of the decision.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: A cross-product interface decision, for example, requires stronger evidence and ownership than a product-internal implementation detail.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: The decision should be linked to the relevant architecture artifacts.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: Enterprise-impacting decisions should reference applicable guardrails or reference architectures.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: Solution-impacting decisions should reference the solution baseline, product participation map, interface catalogue or data flow model.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: Product-impacting decisions should reference the Product Architecture Document, ADR Register, Interface Specification, Product Security Concept or Verification Evidence.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: Where the decision creates risk, deviation or incomplete evidence, this must be made visible.

proposals.title: BAPO Architecture Decision Template
proposals.statement: The decision should not be treated as accepted architecture if critical ownership, process or evidence gaps remain unresolved.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: Enterprise guardrails shall be written so that Solution and Product Architects can apply them without needing interpretation from the original author.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: A guardrail must clearly state why it exists, where it applies, what is mandatory, what can still be decided locally, which evidence is required, who owns it and how exceptions are handled.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: Its purpose is to define the minimum architecture alignment required where inconsistent local decisions would create cross-division fragmentation, integration risk, security gaps, data incompatibility, technology divergence, platform fragmentation or release incompatibility.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: Every enterprise guardrail shall have a clear owner and review mechanism.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: A guardrail must therefore be treated as a living architecture asset that is versioned, communicated, applied, measured and improved through feedback from solutions and products.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: The table below should be used when creating or updating an enterprise guardrail.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: It defines the minimum fields required to make the guardrail understandable, applicable, reviewable and maintainable across Enterprise, Solution and Product Architecture.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: Architecture rule | States the mandatory or recommended architecture guidance. | Required standard, reference architecture, interface rule, data rule, technology rule, security rule, runtime rule or DevSecOps rule

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: Process requirement | Defines how the guardrail is applied, verified and governed. | Required review, checklist, test, KPI, release rule, governance step, quality gate or DevSecOps pipeline evidence

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: A well-written enterprise guardrail should be specific enough to guide architecture decisions, but not so detailed that it unnecessarily constrains product or solution autonomy.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: It should define what must be common while leaving local design freedom where variation does not create enterprise risk.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: The guardrail should also be testable or reviewable.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: Evidence expectations should therefore be stated explicitly.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: However, deviations must be visible, risk-assessed, owned and time-bounded.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: Repeated exceptions should trigger a review of the guardrail itself.

proposals.title: Enterprise Guardrail Template
proposals.statement: An enterprise guardrail should not be considered ready for publication unless the business driver, architecture rule, applicability, ownership, evidence expectation and exception process are clear.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: The Solution Architecture Template shall be used whenever several products must be aligned into one coherent, integrated and releasable solution.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: A solution architecture document shall be updated whenever the solution scope, product participation, capability allocation, interface architecture, data model, security baseline, deployment topology, integration strategy or solution release baseline changes.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: It should be used as a completeness check when several products must be integrated into one releasable solution.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: Each row represents a section or evidence category that should be covered if it affects integration, release compatibility, security, data consistency or operational readiness.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: Section | Purpose | Required content

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: Capability allocation | Shows which product is responsible for which solution capability. | Capability-to-product mapping, responsibility allocation, shared capability ownership, unresolved allocation gaps

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: Architecture runway | Identifies architecture enablers required before integration or release is blocked. | Interface runway, data runway, security runway, platform runway, integration runway, resilience runway

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: The level of detail should be proportional to the solution's complexity and risk.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: A small solution may describe some sections briefly, while a large multi-product solution requires detailed interface, data, security, deployment, release and verification evidence.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: However, no section should be omitted if it affects integration, release compatibility, security, data consistency or operational readiness.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: The Solution Architect owns the solution architecture document and is responsible for keeping it aligned with the solution baseline.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: Product Architects provide the product-level architecture evidence required by the solution, including interface specifications, data contracts, deployment assumptions, security evidence and product release compatibility declarations.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: The template should not be treated as a static document.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: It is a living architecture artifact that must be updated through solution planning, PI planning, integration reviews, demos, release readiness reviews and Inspect & Adapt.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: Changes to participating products, interface versions, data semantics, security assumptions, deployment configuration or verification evidence must be reflected in the solution architecture.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: A solution architecture should not be considered architecture-ready if product participation, capability allocation, cross-product interfaces, data flows, security boundaries, deployment assumptions or ownership are unclear.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Template
proposals.statement: It should not be considered release-ready unless the solution release baseline, product compatibility declarations, integration evidence, security evidence and unresolved risks are current, owned and reviewable.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: The Product Architecture Template shall be used as the standard structure for product-level architecture descriptions.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: It defines the minimum architecture evidence required to understand, review, implement, verify and release an individual product.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: The template may be tailored to product size, maturity and criticality, but the essential evidence categories should remain present.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: The Product Architecture Document should not duplicate low-level design unnecessarily.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: It should focus on architecture-relevant decisions: product contribution, boundaries, building blocks, runtime behavior, deployment assumptions, interfaces, data contracts, quality attributes, security, verification evidence, release compatibility and technical debt.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: It must therefore be current, owned, versioned and aligned with applicable enterprise guardrails and solution baselines.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: It should be used to check whether the product architecture contains the information required for implementation, verification, integration and release readiness.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: Each row represents an architecture evidence category that should be present unless it is clearly not applicable to the product.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: Quality Requirement Catalogue | Defines measurable non-functional requirements. | Performance, determinism, resilience, security, interoperability, deployability, observability, maintainability

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: Product Process Evidence | Shows that required delivery, test, security, release and debt-management mechanisms exist. | CI/CD evidence, test process, release process, security scans, review records, debt-management process

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: The level of detail should be proportional to product complexity, criticality and integration impact.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: A small product may use a compact architecture document, while a product that participates in several solution baselines, exposes critical interfaces, handles sensitive data or supports mission-critical behavior requires stronger evidence.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: The Product Architect owns the Product Architecture Document and is responsible for keeping it consistent with implementation, ADRs, interfaces, data contracts, deployment assumptions, security evidence and release compatibility declarations.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: Security, Data and Platform Architects should contribute where the product affects cross-cutting concerns.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: The Product Architecture Document should be treated as a living artifact.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: It must be updated when major architecture decisions, interfaces, data contracts, security assumptions, deployment models, quality requirements, technical debt or release compatibility change.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: A product architecture should not be considered architecture-ready if the business contribution, context, building blocks, runtime behavior, deployment assumptions, interfaces, quality requirements, security concept or ownership are unclear.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Template
proposals.statement: It should not be considered release-ready unless the required verification evidence, compatibility declaration, security evidence, deployment evidence and open risks are current, owned and reviewable.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: Interface contracts shall be treated as living architecture artifacts.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: An interface contract must be versioned, owned, tested and linked to the relevant product and solution baselines.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: The contract must describe not only the technical structure of an API, topic, event, stream, file or protocol, but also its purpose, provider, consumers, semantics, security assumptions, compatibility rules, error behavior and verification evidence.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: When an interface changes, the affected product architecture, solution architecture and release baselines must be reviewed.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: For critical interfaces, the contract should be supported by automated contract tests so that product teams can release independently while maintaining solution-level compatibility.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: It should be used whenever an interface is consumed by another product, solution, platform, external system or customer environment.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: The interface contract should be detailed enough for another team to implement, consume, test and verify the interface without relying on informal knowledge.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: The contract should therefore describe both the technical exchange format and the expected behavior.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: Interface contracts must be aligned with the Product Architecture Document and the Solution Architecture Document.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: If an interface is part of a solution baseline, its version and compatibility rule must be reflected in the solution release baseline and product release compatibility declarations.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: For critical interfaces, automated contract tests should be mandatory.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: Where automated tests are not yet available, the missing evidence should be captured as product technical debt, solution integration risk or architecture runway.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: An interface change should not be treated as a local product decision if it affects another product, a solution baseline, a data contract, a security boundary, deployment behavior or release compatibility.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: Such changes require impact assessment and, where necessary, Solution Architecture review before release.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: An interface contract should not be considered mature if it is unowned, unversioned, untested, semantically unclear or disconnected from compatibility rules.

proposals.title: Interface Contract Template
proposals.statement: These gaps should be made visible during product architecture reviews, solution architecture reviews and release readiness reviews.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: Data contracts shall be treated as living architecture artifacts.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: A data contract must therefore define not only structure, but also meaning, ownership, classification, provenance, quality expectations, lifecycle rules and permitted use.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: The data contract must explain what the data represents, who owns it, where it comes from, how it was derived, how it may be used, how quality is measured, and which consumers depend on it.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: When a data contract changes, the affected product architecture, solution architecture, data flows, interface contracts and release baselines must be reviewed.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: It should be used whenever data is exchanged, reused, fused, classified, transformed or consumed across products or solutions.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: Metadata | Defines the additional information required to interpret and govern the data. | Timestamp, source identifier, classification, quality indicator, confidence value, version, processing state

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: Classification | Defines security, handling and access restrictions. | Security classification, handling caveats, releasability, access rules, need-to-know constraints, audit requirements

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: A data contract should be detailed enough for another team to consume, validate and interpret the data without relying on informal knowledge.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: The contract should therefore describe both the technical structure and the operational meaning of the data.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: Data contracts must be aligned with the Product Architecture Document and the Solution Architecture Document.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: If a data contract is part of a solution baseline, its version and compatibility rule must be reflected in the solution release baseline and product release compatibility declarations.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: For critical data contracts, validation should be automated where possible.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: Schema validation proves structural correctness, but semantic and quality validation are also required where incorrect meaning, stale data, missing provenance or poor confidence could affect mission outcome, AI behavior, sensor fusion, operational picture quality or release readiness.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: A data contract change should not be treated as a local product decision if it affects another product, a solution baseline, a data flow, a security classification, an AI model, an operational picture or release compatibility.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: Such changes require impact assessment and, where necessary, Solution Architecture and Data Architecture review before release.

proposals.title: Data Contract Template
proposals.statement: A data contract should not be considered mature if it is unowned, unversioned, semantically unclear, unclassified, untested, missing provenance, or disconnected from lifecycle and compatibility rules.

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: The Quality Marker Template shall be used to define, assess and track Enterprise, Solution, Product and BAPO quality markers.

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: It defines a specific architecture concern, the review question used to assess it, the evidence required at different maturity levels, the accountable owner, the review point, the current score, the findings and the improvement actions required to raise maturity.

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: It should be used when defining new markers or when recording marker assessments during architecture reviews.

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: The template makes clear what is being assessed, which evidence is required, who owns the marker and which actions are needed when gaps are found.

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: Review question | Defines what the reviewer must assess. | Clear review question that can be answered through evidence

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: Criticality | Indicates whether the marker is required for architecture readiness or release readiness. | Critical, release-critical, recommended or informational

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: Required evidence for score 3 | Defines what evidence is needed to consider the concern designed and owned. | Architecture description, owner assignment, ADR, mapping, review record, planned process or backlog item

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: Required evidence for score 4 | Defines what evidence is needed to consider the concern verified. | Test result, integration evidence, security evidence, release evidence, deployment evidence, compatibility declaration

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: Required evidence for score 5 | Defines what evidence is needed to consider the concern continuously measured and improved. | KPI trend, runtime metric, operational evidence, repeated review result, improvement action, feedback loop

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: A quality marker should be written so that different reviewers can apply it consistently.

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: The review question must be specific enough to avoid subjective interpretation, and the evidence requirements must make clear what is needed for score 3, score 4 and score 5.

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: A marker should not receive a higher score unless the evidence supports that maturity level.

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: Quality marker assessments should always lead to action when gaps are found.

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: A low score is not only a finding; it should trigger an architecture enabler, technical debt item, verification action, exception request, guardrail update or release-readiness follow-up.

proposals.title: Quality Marker Template
proposals.statement: The template should be used consistently across Enterprise, Solution, Product and BAPO markers.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists
proposals.statement: The checklists should be used as review aids, not as mechanical approval forms.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists
proposals.statement: They help reviewers confirm whether the required business context, architecture decisions, process implications, ownership and evidence are available.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists
proposals.statement: Findings from these reviews should be converted into backlog items, architecture enablers, technical debt items, exceptions, release-readiness actions or guardrail updates.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Enterprise Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Use this checklist when an architecture item may require enterprise-level guidance, guardrails or governance.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Enterprise Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: If the topic is purely local to one product or solution, it should normally remain with Product or Solution Architecture.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Enterprise Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Review question | Purpose | Required evidence or output

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Enterprise Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Is an enterprise guardrail required? | Clarifies whether the issue requires a common rule, standard, reference architecture or governance mechanism. | Guardrail proposal, architecture impact analysis, exception pattern, risk assessment

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Enterprise Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Are process implications defined? | Ensures that the guardrail can be applied, reviewed, tested, governed and improved. | Review process, exception process, KPI tracking, release rule, quality gate, DevSecOps requirement

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Enterprise Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Is the required evidence defined? | Makes enterprise alignment reviewable instead of assumption-based. | Evidence checklist, adoption evidence, review record, KPI dashboard, exception register

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Enterprise Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: What follow-up action is required? | Converts the review into executable governance, backlog or improvement action. | Guardrail update, architecture runway item, portfolio action, exception decision, technical debt item, owner assignment

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Solution Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Use this checklist when several products must work together as one solution.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Solution Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Are architecture runway items identified? | Ensures that required enablers are planned before they become integration or release blockers. | Architecture runway, enabler backlog, dependency map, PI planning input

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Solution Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: What follow-up action is required? | Converts review findings into executable work instead of leaving them as observations. | Product backlog item, solution enabler, technical debt item, exception request, release-readiness action

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Product Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Are quality attributes measurable and evidenced? | Ensures that performance, determinism, resilience, observability, maintainability and deployability claims can be verified. | Quality Requirement Catalogue, test results, measurements, runtime evidence, observability evidence

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Product Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Does the product change affect solution architecture? | Determines whether a product-level change requires solution-level review. | ADR impact assessment, interface change record, data contract change, security impact, runtime or deployment impact

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / Product Architecture Review Checklist
proposals.statement: What follow-up action is required? | Converts review findings into executable backlog, evidence or governance actions. | Product backlog item, architecture enabler, technical debt item, exception request, solution review request

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / System Demo and Inspect & Adapt Feedback Capture Checklist
proposals.statement: It captures what was observed, which architecture claim was affected, which level or artifact is impacted, and which follow-up action is required.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / System Demo and Inspect & Adapt Feedback Capture Checklist
proposals.statement: The checklist shall be used when demo, integration, operational or Inspect & Adapt findings are architecture-relevant.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / System Demo and Inspect & Adapt Feedback Capture Checklist
proposals.statement: It is not required for every minor implementation defect.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / System Demo and Inspect & Adapt Feedback Capture Checklist
proposals.statement: It is required when a finding affects architecture decisions, interfaces, data contracts, security, deployment, release compatibility, quality markers, technical debt, guardrails or solution baselines.

proposals.title: Architecture Review Checklists / System Demo and Inspect & Adapt Feedback Capture Checklist
proposals.statement: Each relevant finding must identify the architecture claim being assessed, the evidence observed, the affected level, the affected artifact, the required follow-up action, the owner and the review point.

proposals.title: Release Readiness Review Checklist
proposals.statement: It is an architecture governance checkpoint that verifies whether the required architecture evidence is complete and whether remaining risks are visible and accepted.

proposals.title: Release Readiness Review Checklist
proposals.statement: The review must distinguish between product release readiness and solution release readiness.

proposals.title: Release Readiness Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Therefore, product compatibility declarations, interface versions, data contract versions, security assumptions, deployment configurations and verification evidence must be assessed against the relevant solution baseline.

proposals.title: Release Readiness Review Checklist
proposals.statement: The Release Readiness Review should not be the first point at which missing evidence is discovered.

proposals.title: Release Readiness Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Critical evidence should be planned during architecture reviews, PI planning, integration planning and verification activities.

proposals.title: Release Readiness Review Checklist
proposals.statement: The release review should confirm readiness, identify remaining risks and decide whether the release can proceed, not create the architecture baseline from scratch.

proposals.title: Release Readiness Review Checklist
proposals.statement: A release should not be approved if critical architecture evidence is missing, outdated, unowned or not traceable to the relevant product or solution baseline.

proposals.title: Release Readiness Review Checklist
proposals.statement: If release proceeds with known gaps, those gaps must be documented as accepted residual risk, architecture exception, technical debt or follow-up action with a named owner and review date.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Both parts should be used together whenever a product, solution or architecture decision deviates from an approved guardrail, baseline, standard or quality expectation.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: The Architecture Exception Template shall be used whenever a product, solution, initiative or architecture decision deviates from an approved enterprise guardrail, standard, reference architecture, solution baseline, interface rule, data rule, security expectation, runtime assumption or quality marker requirement.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: The template must therefore make clear what is being deviated from, why the deviation is needed, what impact it creates, who owns the risk, how the risk is mitigated, how long the exception is valid, and when it must be reviewed again.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: The table below defines the minimum fields required to document an architecture exception.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: It creates the persistent exception record and should be completed before the exception is reviewed or used as release evidence.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: Business reason | Explains why the exception is needed. | Customer constraint, mission need, delivery urgency, legacy dependency, contractual requirement, technology limitation or product-line reason

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: BAPO implications | Shows whether the deviation affects business intent, architecture alignment, delivery process or ownership. | Business priority, architecture risk, required process change, affected owner, governance implication

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: Conditions | Defines additional requirements attached to the approval. | Required evidence, mitigation before release, additional review, migration before next baseline, monitoring requirement

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: The exception template should be completed with enough detail to allow the decision to be reviewed later without relying on informal knowledge.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: A reviewer should be able to understand what was approved, why it was approved, which risk was accepted, which mitigation was required, who owns the follow-up and when the exception expires.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: Approved exceptions must remain visible until they are closed, expired or renewed.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: They should be linked to the relevant exception register, technical debt register, release-readiness record, product compatibility declaration, solution baseline or enterprise guardrail.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: An exception without an owner, mitigation and review date should not be considered governed.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: Conditional approvals must state the conditions explicitly.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: If the conditions are not met, the exception should not be used as valid release evidence.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: Repeated exceptions should be treated as architecture feedback.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Template
proposals.statement: In such cases, the exception should trigger guardrail review, architecture runway, technical debt reduction or portfolio-level improvement action.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: It is an explicit architecture risk decision that must be documented, assessed, owned, time-bounded and reviewed.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: However, each exception must explain why the deviation is needed, what impact it creates, how the risk is mitigated, who owns it and when it will be reviewed again.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: The table below defines the review content required to decide whether an exception can be approved, rejected, conditionally approved, escalated or returned for rework.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: It should be used by the responsible architect, review forum or Architecture Review Board to ensure that the deviation is justified, risk-assessed, owned and time-bounded.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: The following content shall be provided for an Architecture Exception Review:

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Business reason | Explains why the deviation is needed. | Customer constraint, mission need, delivery urgency, business priority, legacy dependency, contractual requirement or product-line reason

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: BAPO implications | Shows whether the deviation affects business intent, architecture alignment, process execution or ownership. | Business priority, architecture risk, required process change, affected owner, governance implication

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: The Architecture Exception Review should determine whether the deviation is acceptable for the affected scope and timeframe.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Major deviations should be reviewed by the Architecture Review Board or the responsible enterprise architecture governance body.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: An approved exception must always remain visible until it is closed, expired or renewed.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: It should be recorded in the relevant exception register and linked to any affected technical debt item, release-readiness decision, product compatibility declaration, solution baseline or enterprise guardrail.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: The exception record should make clear whether the deviation is temporary, conditionally accepted or a candidate for future guardrail improvement.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: Conditional approvals should define explicit conditions.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: If the conditions are not met, the exception should not be treated as valid release evidence.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: If multiple products or solutions request similar deviations, the review should not only approve or reject the individual case.

proposals.title: Architecture Exception Template and Review Checklist / Architecture Exception Review Checklist
proposals.statement: It should also ask whether the underlying enterprise guardrail, solution baseline, platform capability, interface standard or process expectation is incomplete, outdated, too restrictive or insufficiently supported.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: In both cases, compatibility must be declared against a specific baseline.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: A release should not simply claim to be “compatible” in general.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: A product release should not be accepted into a solution release baseline unless its compatibility declaration is complete, current, owned and verified with evidence.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: It should be used whenever a product or solution release declares compatibility with a solution baseline, enterprise baseline, security baseline, platform baseline or deployment baseline.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: The declaration should be treated as release evidence and must be current, owned and supported by verification evidence.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: Security baseline | Confirms alignment with required security assumptions. | Identity model, authentication, authorization, crypto, logging, audit, trust-zone compatibility, security exceptions

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: Approval | Confirms accountable ownership and acceptance. | Product Owner, Product Architect, Solution Architect, Security Architect where required, approval date

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: The declaration should be created or updated whenever a release changes externally visible interfaces, data contracts, deployment assumptions, security behavior, runtime dependencies, compatibility rules or baseline participation.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: A stale declaration should not be accepted as release evidence.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: For product releases, the Product Architect is responsible for the architectural correctness of the declaration.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: For solution releases, the Solution Architect is responsible for confirming that the solution baseline is complete and that all participating product releases are compatible with it.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: A declaration should not be considered complete if it lacks baseline version, interface version, data model version, security assumption, deployment configuration, verification evidence, known limitations or accountable approval.

proposals.title: Release Compatibility Declaration Template
proposals.statement: Missing or incomplete compatibility evidence should be treated as a release-readiness risk, technical debt item, architecture exception or release blocker, depending on severity.
